Documents

Source: vignettes/documents.Rmd
documents.Rmd

A document can display a 3D plot as a static figure or an interactive viewer. This article uses knitr’s output switching, supplies accessible descriptions and arranges plots on a page. Quarto’s R engine uses the same chunk options. Installation is covered in Get started; HTML viewers also need htmlwidgets and svglite, described in Interactive viewing.

A static figure

The motor-car data record weight in thousands of pounds, fuel economy in miles per US gallon and gross horsepower. Printing the plot uses its chosen scene backend and the document’s graphics device. The default backend draws vector geometry; this article’s SVG device keeps those paths scalable.

p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg, z = hp)) +
  geom_point_3d(size = 3, colour = PAL["blue"]) + coord_3d() +
  labs(x = "weight", y = "mpg", z = "horsepower")
p

HTML, PDF and Word

Set the chunk option view3d = TRUE to embed the interactive viewer in HTML. The following chunk runs that switch. The figure dimensions are in inches, and become widget dimensions at 96 pixels per inch. Facet panels, titles, strips and legends follow the plot’s layout.

p

For PDF and Word output, that same option draws a static vector scene. The document device determines the image format: a PDF device retains vector geometry for a PDF document, and a PNG device samples it into pixels for Word. With view3d = FALSE, the chunk uses the backend configured on the plot.

Quarto accepts the equivalent option in its cell metadata. This is the same plot object created above.


``` r
p
```

Accessible descriptions

alt_text_3d() describes the layer types, mapped variables and initial camera angles. The generated description supplies the default alternative text for static figures and an accessible group name around HTML viewers. Inspect it before adding words about what the figure communicates.

alt_text_3d(p)
#> [1] "3D plot. Layers: Point (x = wt, y = mpg, z = hp). Camera: azimuth -60 degrees, elevation 30 degrees, roll 0 degrees; orthographic projection."

An explicit chunk fig.alt takes precedence. A description supplied by labs(alt = ...) takes precedence over the generated layer description. The example below describes the relationship the reader can inspect in the motor-car plot.

described <- p + labs(alt = paste(
  "Motor cars plotted by weight, fuel economy and horsepower.",
  "Heavier cars generally have lower fuel economy."))
alt_text_3d(described)
#> [1] "Motor cars plotted by weight, fuel economy and horsepower. Heavier cars generally have lower fuel economy."

When a chunk prints several plots, supply a vector of descriptions in their printed order. Each static figure gets its own alternative text.

p

p + coord_3d(azimuth = 30)
#> Coordinate system already present. Adding coord_3d() replaces it.

Composing plots

patchwork arranges ggplot objects. Each 3D scene compiles at the physical size of its panel, so camera projection and mark sizes follow the final layout. Stack the plot above a second view to give each one the document column’s width.

other <- p + coord_3d(azimuth = 30)
#> Coordinate system already present. Adding coord_3d() replaces it.
patchwork::wrap_plots(p, other, ncol = 1)

cowplot also preserves the independent scenes. Its composition below contains a 3D view and a 2D view of the same cars. These arrangements are static figures; use a faceted ggplot with the viewer for a live multi-panel document.

flat <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg)) +
  geom_point(colour = PAL["blue"], size = 3) + labs(x = "weight", y = "mpg")
cowplot::plot_grid(p, flat, ncol = 1)

Combining 2D and 3D graphics shows shared scales and plots placed on planes inside a scene.

Saving a raster figure

Choose the scene sampling resolution on the backend, then set the saved image’s pixel dimensions through the device resolution. Both settings use the intended physical size. The temporary file below is six inches wide and four inches high at 144 dots per inch.

raster <- p + coord_3d(backend = backend_3d("raster", dpi = 144))
#> Coordinate system already present. Adding coord_3d() replaces it.
path <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
ggsave(path, raster, width = 6, height = 4, dpi = 144)
file.info(path)$size > 0
#> [1] TRUE
unlink(path)

Output backends explains the rendering choices. Exporting plots and scenes writes model files and native SVG, TikZ or Asymptote output.
